def remove_dirty_chars(s1: str, s2: str) -> str:
    """
    Removes characters from string s1 that are present in string s2.
    
    Args:
        s1 (str): The source string to clean.
        s2 (str): The set of dirty characters to remove.
        
    Returns:
        str: A new string with specified characters removed.
    """
    # Convert the second string into a set for O(1) lookup time
    chars_to_remove = set(s2)
    
    # Use list comprehension to filter s1, keeping only characters NOT in the set
    result_list = [char for char in s1 if char not in chars_to_remove]
    
    return "".join(result_list)

# Test case from your example
if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert remove_dirty_chars("probasscurve", "pros") == 'bacuve'
    print("Test passed!")

def remove_dirty_chars(s1: str, s2: str) -> str:
    """
    Removes characters from string s1 that are present in string s2.
    
    Args:
        s1 (str): The source string to clean.
        s2 (str): The set of dirty characters to remove.
        
    Returns:
        str: A new string with specified characters removed.
    """
    # Convert the second string into a set for O(1) lookup time
    chars_to_remove = set(s2)
    
    # Use list comprehension to filter s1, keeping only characters NOT in the set
    result_list = [char for char in s1 if char not in chars_to_remove]
    
    return "".join(result_list)

# Test case from your example
assert remove_dirty_chars("probasscurve", "pros") == 'bacuve'
print("Test passed!")
